issues.legal_issue: Relevant documents obtained from public authorities after the ordinary documentary-evidence stage should normally be received in a pending civil proceeding when offered before arguments are completed, subject to proof and an opportunity for rebuttal.
material_facts: The appellants sought to establish a disputed entitlement to a share of land-acquisition compensation by relying on revenue records bearing on their pre-existing title.
The documents were public records that had not been in the appellants’ possession or custody; they obtained certified copies from revenue authorities.
They applied to produce the documents late, at the stage of arguments, but before arguments were completed.
The trial court refused to condone the delay and receive the documents, and the High Court upheld that refusal.
issues.conclusion: The refusal was unjustified. The delay was condoned, and the trial court was directed to receive the documents, give the parties an opportunity to prove them and, if necessary, allow rebuttal before deciding the reference.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XIII Rule 1(1) and (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, parties are to produce documentary evidence in their possession or power at or before settlement of issues, with the prescribed list. Where documents were not in a party’s possession or custody, an application may be made to condone delay in filing them; the explanation required is not as rigorous as under Section 5 of the Limitation Act. The Court relied on the principle associated with Order XLI Rule 27 CPC that an appellate court may receive relevant documents when the interests of justice require it, and held that documents sought to be produced in the trial court before arguments are completed should normally be received if relevant, with an opportunity to prove them and rebut them. The Court also relied on the relevance of the records to the real issue in controversy.

rule.if: pending_civil_reference and documents_bear_on_disputed_title and documents_were_outside_proponent_custody and certified_copies_obtained_from_public_authority and documents_offered_late_but_before_arguments_closed

predicates.pending_civil_reference: The documents were offered in a pending civil proceeding to resolve a dispute over entitlement to compensation.
predicates.documents_bear_on_disputed_title: The documents contained records relevant to a party’s asserted pre-existing title and claimed share.
predicates.documents_were_outside_proponent_custody: The documents had not been in the offering party’s possession or custody.
predicates.certified_copies_obtained_from_public_au: The offering party obtained certified copies of the public records from the responsible public authority.
predicates.documents_offered_late_but_before_argume: The offering party sought to produce the documents after the ordinary documentary-evidence stage but before arguments were completed.

issues.definition: When a party in a pending civil reference offers relevant certified public records obtained outside its custody after the ordinary filing stage but before arguments close, the records are received subject to proof and rebuttal.
